definitions.gloss: the morning after an all-nighter; post-all-nighter state
definitions.explanation: The period immediately following a night spent without sleep, typically the next morning or day. Implies tiredness and exhaustion from staying up all night, whether for work, study, or other reasons.

examples.japanese: {徹夜明|てつやあ}けで{頭|あたま}がぼんやりする。
examples.english: My head is foggy after pulling an all-nighter.

examples.japanese: {徹夜明|てつやあ}けのまま{会議|かいぎ}に{出|で}なければならなかった。
examples.english: I had to attend the meeting without having slept at all.

examples.japanese: {徹夜明|てつやあ}けで{運転|うんてん}するのは{危険|きけん}だから、{少|すこ}しでも{仮眠|かみん}を{取|と}った{方|ほう}がいい。
examples.english: Driving after an all-nighter is dangerous, so you should at least take a short nap.

notes:
USAGE:
{徹夜明|てつやあ}け is a compound of {徹夜|てつや} (all-nighter) and {明|あ}け (the period after). It is used as a noun, often followed by で to indicate doing something in the post-all-nighter state. Common among students and workers.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {徹夜明|てつやあ}けで + verb (to do something after an all-nighter)
- {徹夜明|てつやあ}けのまま (still in the all-nighter aftermath)
- {徹夜明|てつやあ}けの{体|からだ} (a body exhausted from an all-nighter)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {徹夜明|てつやあ}け: state after staying up all night
- {徹夜|てつや}: staying up all night (the act itself)
- {夜更|よふ}かし: staying up late (not necessarily all night)
- {寝不足|ねぶそく}: lack of sleep (general sleep deprivation)
